findings.claim: The round-2 repair replaced R5's overstatement with a narrower one of the same species: the new source comment asserts unqualified that "Item 6 was the LAST unpinned entry in this table", but ALIAS_FROM["4"] can still be moved by years, relabel four committed fixtures, and leave _demo, the fast suite and the invariant suite all green — the 1990/2099 sweep the claim rests on only proves the extremes are caught, not the band in between.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/segment.py:654 (`# Item 6 was the LAST unpinned entry in this table (PR #17 R5)`), added by 32915d4; same generalization at tasks/TODO.md:73 ("all eight are now pinned") and prompts/010-t14-taxonomy-completeness-and-10ka.md:184 ("none uncaught") — those two at least carry the sweep's parenthetical, the source comment carries none. Counterexample: ALIAS_FROM["4"] = date(2016,1,1) (or date(2013,12,31), or date(2010,1,31)) is not an extreme value and is caught by nothing. Because segment.py:177 makes item 4's Reserved window run `date(2010,1,1) <= period_end < ALIAS_FROM["4"]`, moving the constant to 2016-01-01 renders item 4 as "Reserved" instead of "Mine Safety Disclosures" on msft-2013, spatz-2014, cvx-2015 and reac-2015; moving it to 2010-01-31 renders wmt-2010's item 4 as "Mine Safety Disclosures" instead of "Reserved". Measured: _demo GREEN, fast 51/51 = 1.000, invariant 13/13 = 1.000 for all three values. A programmatic scan of every ALIAS_FROM key against every fixture period end (and +/-1 day) shows "5","6","10","12","13","15" have zero output-changing mutations that survive _demo, while "4" has many — so "4", not "6", is the entry the coverage claim should be hedged around.
